stem: Which tool is used to cut metal such as a steel bar?

options.content: Hacksaw
options.rationale: Correct: its fine teeth cut metal.

options.content: Crosscut saw
options.rationale: A crosscut saw cuts timber across the grain.

options.content: Rip saw
options.rationale: A rip saw cuts timber along the grain.

options.content: Bow saw
options.rationale: A bow saw cuts logs and branches.

explanation: Hacksaws have fine, hardened teeth for metal.

stem: Why are the teeth of a saw "set" (bent alternately left and right)?

options.content: So the cut is wider than the blade and the saw does not stick
options.rationale: Correct: the blade runs freely in the kerf.

options.content: So the saw can cut equally well on the push and the pull stroke
options.rationale: Setting does not create two-way cutting.

options.content: To make the teeth stronger against rusting
options.rationale: Setting has no effect on rust.

options.content: To make the saw lighter to carry
options.rationale: Mass hardly changes.

explanation: Without set, the blade binds in the cut.

stem: Which hand tool is best for lifting potatoes and turning a compost heap?

options.content: Rake
options.rationale: A rake levels and collects trash.

options.content: Digging fork
options.rationale: Correct: its tines lift without cutting tubers.

options.content: Slasher
options.rationale: A slasher cuts grass.

options.content: Screwdriver
options.rationale: A screwdriver drives screws.

explanation: Forks penetrate heavy soil and lift tubers with less damage than a spade.

stem: The nozzle of a knapsack sprayer is blocked during spraying. What should the operator do?

options.content: Blow through the nozzle with the mouth to clear it
options.rationale: This puts pesticide into the body.

options.content: Remove it with gloves on and clean it with a soft brush or grass stalk
options.rationale: Correct: safe and does not damage the nozzle.

options.content: Push a piece of wire through the hole
options.rationale: Wire damages the nozzle opening and spray pattern.

options.content: Pump the pressure up as high as possible until the blockage is forced out
options.rationale: This can burst seals and does not clear dirt reliably.

explanation: Never blow through nozzles; clean gently and wear PPE.
hints: Think of safety and of the nozzle's opening.

stem: Why should a farmer keep a separate knapsack sprayer for herbicides?

options.content: Herbicides cannot be sprayed through a normal knapsack nozzle
options.rationale: Normal nozzles can spray herbicides.

options.content: Insecticides make herbicides stronger
options.rationale: This is not the reason.

options.content: Traces of herbicide left in the tank can damage crops later
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Herbicide sprayers must be painted a special colour
options.rationale: Colour is not the reason.

explanation: Residues of herbicide are hard to remove completely and can injure the next crop sprayed.
hints: What does a herbicide do to plants?

stem: Why must a file always be fitted with a handle?

options.content: Files cut only when they have a handle
options.rationale: The teeth cut either way, but it is unsafe.

options.content: The handle keeps the teeth sharp
options.rationale: Handles do not sharpen.

options.content: The pointed tang could pierce the user's hand
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The handle stops the file rusting
options.rationale: Rust is prevented by keeping it dry.

explanation: A bare tang can be driven into the palm on the forward stroke.

stem: A bolt head on a plough is becoming rounded because the farmer's spanner slips. What is the most likely cause?

options.content: The spanner has been oiled
options.rationale: Oiling the tool is normal care.

options.content: The farmer pulled the spanner towards himself as he turned it
options.rationale: Pulling is the safe way to use a spanner.

options.content: The bolt is made of galvanised steel
options.rationale: Galvanising does not cause rounding.

options.content: The spanner is the wrong size for the bolt head
options.rationale: Correct: an oversized spanner slips and rounds the corners.

explanation: Use the exact size of spanner and pull steadily.
hints: What happens if the jaws are loose on the head?

stem: After spraying, Tatenda has 2 L of rinse water from cleaning the knapsack tank. What is the safest way to dispose of it?

options.content: Pour it into the nearest stream so that it is diluted
options.rationale: This pollutes water and harms fish and people.

options.content: Pour it down the toilet in the farmhouse
options.rationale: It may reach water sources and is unsafe.

options.content: Give it to the cattle to drink
options.rationale: Very dangerous to animals.

options.content: Spray it over the crop area that was just treated
options.rationale: Correct: the dilute chemical stays where it was meant to be.

explanation: Rinsate is sprayed onto the treated crop, never into water or drains.
hints: Where can the chemical do least harm?

stem: A claw hammer can both drive nails and pull them out.
explanation: True. The claw grips the nail head for removal.

stem: A screwdriver may be used as a small chisel or lever if no other tool is available.
explanation: False. This damages the tip and can cause injury; use the correct tool.

stem: Match each knapsack sprayer part with its function.

right.content: Turns the spray on and off
Keeps dirt out of the tank

explanation: Know the parts of a knapsack sprayer in order.

stem: Match each tool with its main use.

right.content: Cutting grass for a fire guard
Levelling a seedbed to a fine tilth

explanation: Choose the right tool for the job.

stem: Complete the sentence.

payload.template: Filings are cleaned from the teeth of a file with a file {{blank:a}}; a loose hammer head is tightened by driving in a {{blank:b}}.

explanation: File card; wedge.

stem: Assume a good-quality hoe costs US\$12 and lasts 6 years, and a cheap hoe costs US\$5 and lasts 2 years. Calculate the cost per year of the cheap hoe, in US dollars.
explanation: US\$5 ÷ 2 = US\$2.50 a year, compared with US\$12 ÷ 6 = US\$2 for the good hoe, which is cheaper in the long run.
workedSolution: 1. US\$5 ÷ 2 = US\$2.50 a year, compared with US\$12 ÷ 6 = US\$2 for the good hoe, which is cheaper in the long run.

stem: Name the type of saw with a curved metal frame used to cut logs and prune branches.
explanation: A **bow saw**.

stem: Name the part of a knapsack sprayer that breaks the liquid into droplets.
explanation: The **nozzle**.

stem: Describe how a knapsack sprayer should be cleaned and stored after spraying an insecticide.

points.description: Rinse the tank three times with clean water (wearing PPE).
Spray the rinse water through the lance onto the treated crop, not into water sources.
Clean the filter and nozzle; check washers and seals and oil moving parts.
Store empty, dry and open to air, locked away from food, children and animals.

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Wearing gloves, rinse the tank three times and spray the rinse water through the lance over the treated crop. Clean the filter and nozzle, check the seals and oil the pump, then store the sprayer empty and dry in a locked store away from food and children.

explanation: Rinse, flush, maintain, store.

stem: Explain **two** safety rules for using cultivation hand tools on a school farm.

points.description: Carry sharp tools with the blade pointing down.
So that people are not cut if the carrier trips or turns.
Never leave rakes or forks lying with the points upward / keep a safe distance when swinging picks and slashers.
So nobody steps on the points or is struck by the swinging tool (also: check heads are tight so they do not fly off).

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Sharp tools are carried with the blades pointing down so nobody is cut if the carrier trips. Rakes are never left with the teeth upward, because someone could step on them and be injured or hit by the handle.

explanation: Rule plus reason.

stem:
A teacher checks the farm tool store at the end of term.

| Tool | Condition found in the store |
| --- | --- |
| Saw | Blade rusty; teeth blunt; cut binds in the wood |
| File | No handle; teeth clogged with metal filings |
| Knapsack sprayer | Nozzle blocked; tank still contains herbicide mixture |
| Hoe | Blade blunt; handle loose and split |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe how the saw should be restored.

points.description: Remove rust (wire brush or emery) and oil the blade.
Sharpen the teeth with a (triangular) file and reset them so the saw does not bind.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe what should be done with the file.

points.description: Fit a handle before using it again.
Clean the teeth with a file card (wire brush) and store it apart from other tools.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Describe how the sprayer should be dealt with.

points.description: Wearing PPE, empty the mixture safely onto the target area and rinse the tank three times.
Clean the nozzle with a soft brush (not by blowing) and store the sprayer dry and locked away.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Describe how the hoe should be repaired.

points.description: Sharpen the blade with a file.
Replace the split handle and fix the head firmly (wedge).

explanation: Maintenance of workshop tools, sprayers and cultivation tools.
hints: Give the maintenance needed for each fault.

stem: Rudo is starting a vegetable garden on hard, stony ground and will build a fowl run from gum poles and wire. She has a small budget for tools and must protect her crops from aphids.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Suggest **three** cultivation tools Rudo needs to prepare the garden, giving the use of each.

points.description: Pick (or mattock) to break the hard, stony ground.
Digging fork or hoe to dig and loosen the soil / spade to dig and mix compost.
Rake to level the bed and make a fine tilth.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Suggest **three** workshop tools for building the fowl run, giving the use of each.

points.description: Bow saw or crosscut saw to cut poles and timber to length.
Claw hammer to drive (and pull) nails or staples.
Pliers/spanner/screwdriver to fix wire, bolts or screws on the door.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Name **two** items of protective clothing she should wear when spraying the aphids.

points.description: Gloves / overalls with long sleeves.
Goggles or face shield / mask / boots.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Discuss whether Rudo should buy cheap tools or fewer, better-quality tools.

points.description: Cheap tools cost less now, so she can buy more of them with a small budget.
But they wear, bend or break quickly, and replacements and lost work cost more over time.
Good tools last longer, are safer and cost less per year of use if maintained.
Judgement: buy fewer, good-quality essential tools and maintain them (borrow or share others).

explanation: Choosing, using and buying tools for a new garden and structure.
hints: Choose tools for each job and justify them.
